newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN REJECTS ALL BIDS IN 26-WEEK T-BILLS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN REJECTS ALL BIDS IN 26-WEEK T-BILLS.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Wednesday rejected all bids in an auction of 26-week treasury bills, the central bank (NBS) said in a statement.
The statement said bids totalled 250 million crowns but no further details were released.
Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment on the auction.
Banks have been demanding high yields in state securities auctions due to an accute crown liquidity shortage on the local money market which has pushed interest rates up.
The Slovak interbank rates at present hover above 30 percent.
The Finance Ministry said it would issue on Thursday a special 3.009 billion crown tranche of one-week treasury bills to the NBS's portfolio at an undisclosed rate.

Several times the NBS has this year helped refinance the state budget deficit during liquidity crunches on the local money market. By law, the central bank can hold state securities totalling to up to eight percent of overall 1996 budget revenues.

Finance Ministry uses T-bills and state bonds as its main tolls to cover state budget deficit, which totalled 4.692 billion crowns in the first four months of this year, up from 3.450 billion crowns in the first quarter of 1997.
